title: forbidden_pattern kind: rules parsing + query validation
description:
Add `ForbiddenPattern { language, query }` to ConstraintKind in src/rules.rs. TOML fields: kind="forbidden_pattern", language (required), query (required, tree-sitter S-expression), plus shared name/severity/scope/provenance. Compile the query against the declared language's grammar at parse_rules time — compilation failure becomes a constraint parse error (existing constraint_parse_errors channel), not a runtime surprise. Severity default: Advisory. Identity: blake3(kind_tag, language, query, scope). Scope reuses scope_matches_path (glob-or-prefix, sutra/238/239).

Grammar selection needs a language-name → tree_sitter::Language mapping — check the existing parser registry/adapter layer before inventing one.

Design: sutra/221 implementation_plan. Tests in src/rules.rs #[cfg(test)] following the existing 22-test pattern (parsing, identity, defaults, invalid query error, unknown language error).
execution_record: Used LanguageRegistry::adapter_for_language + grammar() for query validation as directed. Threaded the registry internally through all_constraints → into_constraint (no public API change). Had to add ForbiddenPattern arms to 3 exhaustive matches in constraints/mod.rs, tools/constraints.rs, and tools/orient.rs. 12 new tests covering parsing, defaults, required fields, unknown language, invalid query, identity determinism, and scope interaction.

messages.author: agent
messages.text: Review: approve with notes. Codex adversarial review found no defects in the rules parsing implementation. The two findings (engine not wired into production evaluators; symbol-scoped waivers can't match) are both out-of-scope — covered by sutra/242 and sutra/243 respectively. Minor note: all_constraints() now unconditionally creates default_registry() even when no forbidden_pattern constraints exist — small allocation (4 unit structs) but unnecessary overhead for workspaces without pattern rules. Consider lazy creation if profiling shows it matters."
